sources.news_title: Where in the world is Flávio Bolsonaro?
sources.text:
Brazil's former presidential candidate is reportedly headed to the United States, days after Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered him to surrender his passports.
Flávio Bolsonaro has reportedly fled to the United States after narrowly losing Brazil's presidential election under unusual circumstances and after Brazil's left-wing government demanded he surrender his passports.
Bolsonaro, son of convicted former President Jair Bolsonaro, has left Brazil for the U.S., two sources told CNN Tuesday. A U.S. official then seemingly confirmed the report, telling the outlet that Bolsonaro was headed for Florida before stating that his destination was unclear, CNN said.
'Do not recognize these elections.'
Reuters, citing three sources, reported that he had left Brazil for the U.S. One source even said that the Trump administration had granted asylum to Bolsonaro and his immediate family, the outlet reported.
"After months of intense work that has been unfairly thwarted, I am not in the mood to speak to the press," said Paulo Figueiredo, an unofficial family spokesman.
Bolsonaro lost Sunday's runoff to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva by about 3.6 points after Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin extended voting by two hours, stirring fraud suspicions. Zanin was Lula's personal defense lawyer until Lula put him on the court in 2023.
Lula was previously found guilty of corruption and money-laundering charges. He spent over 550 days in prison before he was freed in 2019. The Supreme Court annulled his convictions in 2021 on jurisdictional grounds.
The elder Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest for what some claim was a political hit job. Flávio Bolsonaro also faces allegations of money laundering and other crimes.
"It is impossible to accept the result of the elections under these conditions," Flávio Bolsonaro said Sunday night, vowing to seek annulment.
RELATED: Feds arrest 6 alleged fraudsters in Maine health care scandal
Mark Wilson/Getty Images
"Do not recognize these elections," Eduardo Bolsonaro, Flávio's brother, said in an X video. On Tuesday, Eduardo called reports that his brother had absconded a "lie," CNN reported.
Justice Alexandre de Moraes signed a sealed order the night of the presidential election demanding that Bolsonaro surrender his passports. The order also prohibited Bolsonaro from leaving Brazil.
Federal Police canceled the passports Tuesday amid reports that Bolsonaro had fled the country, according to CNN.
Argentina's Infobae reported that Bolsonaro crossed into the Misiones province to take a private jet, though this report remains unconfirmed. Argentina said it has "no record" of him entering.
“The process is confidential. We do not have any information,” Brazil's Supreme Court told Blaze News when asked about Moraes' passport confiscation order.
The State Department and U.S. Customs and Border Protection did not respond to Blaze News' requests for comment.

sources.text:
Brazilian politician Flavio Bolsonaro left his country on Tuesday for the United States, US media reported, after he refused to accept defeat in the presidential runoff election held over the weekend.
Bolsonaro, who faces multiple legal challenges, had his passports cancelled but had not surrendered the documents as of Tuesday afternoon. The New York Times, CNN and other outlets reported that he had left Brazil, citing unnamed US officials.
The US State Department said on Tuesday that it would issue visas to Bolsonaro and his family “and allow them entry into the United States” but stopped short of confirming whether they were travelling to the country.
Flavio Bolsonaro is under legal scrutiny in several cases, including a corruption probe into the financing of a biopic about his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest over an alleged plot to stage a coup.

While he cried foul and vowed to challenge the election result in court, his party and allies have accepted the outcome, leaving him increasingly isolated.
The New York Times reported that Bolsonaro was also being investigated over his ties to a Brazilian lawyer accused of laundering more than $1bn through an alleged fraud scheme.
Flavio Bolsonaro’s brother, Eduardo, is based in the United States.
Despite media reports that Bolsonaro had entered neighbouring Argentina, the country’s security ministry and migration authorities denied on Tuesday that this had happened.

Brazils Flavio Bolsonaro reportedly heads to US despite travel ban after election defeat
sources.text:
Brazil's defeated presidential candidate Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro has reportedly left the country for the United States despite a judicial travel ban, with conflicting accounts of his whereabouts emerging Tuesday as authorities investigate a possible escape through Argentina.
Brazilian news outlet Globo cited sources close to Bolsonaro that it said confirmed he had left Brazil with his family, while official channels have not officially confirmed his departure or established his route.
The reports came after Brazil's Federal Police canceled Bolsonaro's regular and diplomatic passports Tuesday when he failed to comply with a court order requiring him to surrender the documents within 24 hours.
Supreme Federal Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes issued the order Monday, a day after Bolsonaro lost the presidential runoff to incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.
The ruling also prohibited the 45-year-old senator from leaving Brazil.
The restrictions stem from an investigation into suspected money laundering and currency evasion involving financial transactions linked to attorney Willer Tomaz, an associate of Bolsonaro.
The senator is also under investigation in a separate case involving the financing of Dark Horse, a biographical film about his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro. Authorities are examining alleged payments connected to Daniel Vorcaro, the former owner of the now-defunct financial institution Banco Master.
Bolsonaro, who denies wrongdoing, said Monday that he had no intention of leaving Brazil.
"I have never thought about leaving the country. I will hand over my passports and defend myself against this travesty," Bolsonaro said, describing the judicial order as "a clear attempt to intimidate me."
He made the remarks after visiting his father, who is serving a 27-year prison sentence under house arrest in Brasilia.
Speculation about his whereabouts intensified Tuesday after Argentine media reported that he had crossed into Argentina by land using his national identity card and planned to board a private flight to Miami with his wife and daughters.
The reports centered on a Gulfstream G400 private jet, registered as LV-JQW and operated by Argentine charter company Baires Fly SA, which arrived at Puerto Iguazu airport near the Brazilian border from Buenos Aires late Monday.
The aircraft had been expected to depart for the US with four passengers and three crew members but remained on the ground Tuesday.
Argentine media reported that aviation authorities had withheld departure clearance over regulatory issues, while other reports indicated that the planned passengers never arrived and the flight was canceled.
However, Argentina's National Directorate of Migration said it had no record of Bolsonaro entering the country and that no flight plan had been submitted listing members of his family.
The agency said authorities had inspected the aircraft and its crew and found the company's documentation in order.
Brazilian federal police also found no record of Bolsonaro leaving the country through an official immigration checkpoint and began examining border crossings and flight records to determine whether he had departed.
Bolsonaro's campaign coordinator, Sen. Rogerio Marinho, initially denied that he had left Brazil, while his brother Eduardo, who lives in the US, dismissed the reports as a "lie."
Bolsonaro's reported departure comes two days after Lula defeated him in Sunday's presidential runoff to secure a fourth term in office.
The senator initially called for the election result to be annulled, although his Liberal Party has acknowledged Lula's victory.

sources.text:

The US Embassy in Brazil did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Bolsonaro’s lawyer also did not respond.
It was not immediately clear where Bolsonaro was heading, when he would arrive or whether he would seek asylum. US President Donald Trump’s administration has previously alleged that Flavio’s father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, was a victim of judicial persecution in Brazil.
Departure threatens to deepen US-Brazil rift
Flavio’s departure for the United States threatens to deepen a rift between the two most populous nations in the Americas.
President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has accused Washington of colluding with the Bolsonaros to return them to power. Reuters reported ahead of Sunday’s election that the US State Department had campaigned to restore them to office.
Passport order follows shock election defeat
Bolsonaro was favoured to win Sunday’s presidential election but suffered a shock defeat to leftist Lula. On Monday, he was given 24 hours to surrender his passports as part of a money laundering probe in which he denies wrongdoing. That deadline has now passed, and his documents have been cancelled, two other sources said.
It was unclear whether he could enter the United States with his passports cancelled.
Jair Bolsonaro’s previous US stay and coup sentence
Jair Bolsonaro also travelled to the United States after refusing to concede defeat to Lula in 2022, when former US President Joe Biden was in office. He eventually returned to Brazil but was later sentenced to 27 years in prison for plotting a coup after his supporters stormed government buildings in Brasilia.
His son has yet to officially concede defeat. On Sunday, he said he would seek to annul the result over alleged voter irregularities. However, his Liberal Party said on Monday that it acknowledged Lula’s victory.
Questions over how Bolsonaro left Brazil

Right-wing influencer Paulo Figueiredo, who serves as an unofficial spokesperson for the Bolsonaro family, declined to answer questions about Bolsonaro’s whereabouts.
“After months of intense work that has been unfairly thwarted, I am not in the mood to speak to the press,” he said in a message. “If I have any comments to make on any matter, I will get in touch.”

sources.news_title: Rumors Claim Flávio Bolsonaro Refused to Hand Over Passports, Fled Brazil
sources.text:
The Brazilian news outlets Metropoles and Jovem Pan reported on Tuesday that Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost a close presidential race against incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva under dubious circumstances, fled the country after authorities attempted to confiscate his passport.
The reports followed a similar claim overnight from the Argentine news network Infobae, which initially reported that Bolsonaro, son of imprisoned former President Jair Bolsonaro, had flown to Argentina en route to the United States. Infobae has since issued an update that the private jet it had first reported would carry Bolsonaro appeared to have canceled its flight.
Bolsonaro lost the second round of presidential voting on Sunday to Lula, who turned 81 on Tuesday and is expecting to govern for at least another four years. The election was marred by controversy after a top court justice, who previously served as Lula’s defense lawyer, issued an unprecedented decree forcibly extending voting hours from 5:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. on Sunday. The order was issued after 5:00 p.m., so only polling stations that had violated orders to close at 5:00 p.m. were allowed to stay open later.
Sen. Bolsonaro had initially stated on Sunday that he would challenge the results of the election and demand a redo. On Monday, he published a video from an undisclosed location asserting that he would not challenge the election, but instead seek a “cassation,” an order deeming Lula and his vice presidential candidate, Geraldo Alckmin, unfit to hold the office of the presidency. Bolsonaro also reportedly denied that he had considered leaving the country.
The senator had also denounced that Lula’s government moved to strip him of his passport hours after the election, allegedly in relation to an investigation into corruption allegations. Lula himself was convicted of misappropriating government funds to buy a luxury beachfront property while he was president in a trial in 2017, but his conviction was overturned on a technicality in 2021, allowing him to run for president again.
According to Metropoles, which cited “people close to the [Bolsonaro] family,” Bolsonaro was at press time, on Tuesday afternoon, on a flight to Florida. It claimed that Sen. Bolsonaro had allegedly gone silent among his peers, and most recently sent a message to campaign manager Rogério Marinho stating that he was “cooling [his] head.” Notably, neither the Bolsonaro camp nor the Brazilian government have confirmed this report, and previous reports on Tuesday insisted that there was no immigration record on file indicating that Sen. Bolsonaro had attempted to leave the country.
Similarly, on Tuesday afternoon local time, Jovem Pan, an online news outlet that skews right, reported that its police sources could confirm Sen. Bolsonaro’s departure from the country. Jovem Pan stated only that its sources, both police and unspecified sources close to the senator, had stated that Sen. Bolsonaro was on a flight to the United States. The outlet did not indicate that Argentina played any role in the departure, nor did Argentine authorities have any record of Sen. Bolsonaro traveling there. The outlet also shared frustration from allies of the senator who said they had attempted to contact him all morning, particularly following the initial rumors of his flight, but were unable to reach him.
“The broadcaster’s report[s] revealed that only members of the hardcore nucleus around the senator had knowledge of his movements,” Jovem Pan claimed. “A great number of his allies were taken by surprise by the news. Among the information circulating regarding Flávio was the possibility of a flight to Argentina before traveling to the United States.”
Prior to these reports, Infobae, an Argentine online news outlet, reported in the early hours of Tuesday that it had reason to believe a private aircraft, identified as a Gulfstream G400, had stopped in Puerto Iguazú, Argentina, and was allegedly preparing to carry Sen. Bolsonaro to Fort Lauderdale, Florida. Infobae later reported, however, that the flight to the United States was canceled due to “the absence of one of the four passengers, according to Airport Security Police.” Both Brazilian and Argentine government officials told Infobae, reportedly, that they had no information indicating that Sen. Bolsonaro had left Brazil or entered Argentina. Online flight trackers also observed that the airplane in question did not leave Puerto Iguazú on Tuesday.
The Brazilian newspaper O Globo reported on Tuesday, similarly, that the Argentine National Immigration Directorate had denied having any record of Sen. Bolsonaro in the country. It also noted, however, that Sen. Bolsonaro had refused to hand over his passports: a regular Brazilian passport, and a diplomatic passport specially issued to senators. Some reports suggested that this led authorities to invalidate the passports, which would in theory make it impossible for Sen. Bolsonaro to use them. Allied nations such as Argentina, where President Javier Milei has yet to congratulate Lula at press time, and America, where President Donald Trump said the Brazilian election “looked rigged,” may be willing to overlook their cancellation in favor of political asylum for a persecuted opposition politician.

Bolsonaro was served with the order to surrender his passports Monday, a day after his stunning loss. Bolsonaro said he received it outside the home where his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest for attempting a coup following his 2022 election loss to Lula. After that defeat, Jair Bolsonaro fled Brazil for Florida. He returned three months later.
The sealed Supreme Court order, viewed by The Associated Press, was issued Sunday. Bolsonaro has refused to concede defeat and has made unsubstantiated allegations of election fraud.
Bolsonaro raises questions about election he lost
Bolsonaro initially asked for the election results to be annulled after an evening of chaos at some polling places that prompted authorities to extend voting by two hours.
On Monday, he urged the electoral court to investigate alleged election fraud and nullify Lula's and Vice President Geraldo Alckmin's candidacies, which the electoral court has never done before.
“I never thought about leaving the country,” Bolsonaro said in a video published on his social media channels. "I will hand over my passports and I will defend myself from this aberration. It is a clear attempt to intimidate me. But I will not be silenced."
To overturn the result, Bolsonaro would have to present evidence of fraud affecting Lula's 4.4 million-vote margin and convince the eight-member electoral court before the results are certified on Dec. 18.
Lula, who turned 81 on Tuesday, received more than 64 million votes, compared with fewer than 60 million for Bolsonaro, a margin of nearly 4%.
Bolsonaro said in a video posted Monday on his social media channels that he had no plans to leave Brazil and instead was attempting to organize opposition among his congressional colleagues to the election results. His eight-year term as a senator expires Jan. 31, 2027, which will also cause him to lose special jurisdiction at the country's Supreme Court.
Bolsonaro is under investigation by Brazil's Supreme Court for alleged corruption, money laundering and tax evasion in two cases. In one, he's accused of using a sports betting company to launder fraudulent deductions from government pensions paid to senior citizens. In the other, he is accused of accepting millions of dollars from a disgraced banker.
He has denied any wrongdoing in both cases, and has claimed Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, who is heading one of the investigations, is a Lula ally. Prosecutors suspect the funds from the banker were used to pay his brother, Eduardo Bolsonaro’s, expenses and to promote Flávio Bolsonaro’s political agenda with the Trump administration, documents show.
Mauricio Marcon, a lawmaker of Bolsonaro’s Liberal Party, also questioned de Moraes’ objectivity on Tuesday. “Seven minutes after the election, Alexandre de Moraes ordered his passports to be seized,” Marcon said. Bolsonaro "will represent us in a free country. He will continue to be our leader."
Brazilians had earlier taken to social media to ask where Bolsonaro was. Reporters gathered outside his home in the capital, Brasilia, but he did not appear.
A spokesperson for the Ministry of Security of Argentina denied reports the Brazilian senator had entered the country. Brazilian media outlets reported that many Bolsonaro allies had been unable to reach him.
Paulo Figueiredo, a close ally of Bolsonaro's who lives in the United States, was asked about the senator's whereabouts and did not answer directly.
“At this moment — following months of intense work that were unfairly thwarted — I have no desire to speak with the press. I kindly ask that you do not persist. Should I have a statement to make on any matter, I will reach out,” Figueiredo said.
